chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Zayd al-Shahham, from an unnamed narrator, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

'Musa ibn Imran (peace be upon him) performed Hajj and with him were seventy prophets from the Children of Israel. The nose-ropes of their camels were made of palm-fibre. They were reciting the Talbiyya, and the mountains were responding to them. Upon Musa were two Qatwani cloaks. He was saying: "Here I am! Your servant, son of Your servant!"'

key_terms.تَلْبِيَة: Talbiyya — the ritual call of Hajj: 'Labbayk Allahumma Labbayk' (Here I am, O God, here I am), recited by pilgrims
key_terms.خُطُم: Nose-ropes/bridles — leads attached to the camel's nose, here made from simple palm-fibre rather than leather, indicating extreme humility
key_terms.عَبَاءَة قَطَوَانِيَّة: Qatwani cloak — a coarse woolen garment from Qatwana, a place near Kufa, symbolizing the pilgrim's simplicity and humility
key_terms.لَبَّيْكَ: Labbayk — 'Here I am (in Your service)', the opening of the Talbiyya
key_terms.يُلَبُّون: They recited the Talbiyya — the present participle emphasizing the continuous nature of the supplication during the pilgrimage

ai.seo_question: Did Prophet Musa perform Hajj? What was the Hajj of Musa ibn Imran like according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Baqir (AS) describes the Hajj of Prophet Musa (Moses, peace be upon him), who performed the pilgrimage accompanied by seventy prophets from the Children of Israel. The vivid details — palm-fibre camel bridles symbolizing humility, mountains echoing the Talbiyya, and Musa's humble supplication — emphasize the spiritual grandeur and antiquity of the Hajj rite. The hadith situates Hajj as an act of worship shared by prophets across generations, reinforcing its divine institution long before Islam.
